O.outcome_detail: alignment of median pupils' IQs with the normal range

result.effect: median IQs ranged from 0.93 to 1.04 across the lowest- and highest-scoring groups in the twelfth year

cells.quote: This criterion is very admirably fulfilled. In the twelfth year, where the discrepancies are the greatest, the median child in the lowest scoring group has an IQ of 0.93, and the median child in the highest scoring group has 1.04 for an IQ. The other deviations from 1.00 are much smaller.
cells.note: The study presents the separate-community method as preferable to lumping results, but does not report a formal statistical comparison.

D.treatment: actual median ages by community and month

O.outcome_detail: accuracy of age-based intelligence standards

cells.quote: It has heretofore been the assumption that the children of a certain age have a median exactly at the half year, that is, for example, the children from 13.0 to 13.99 years old have a median of 13.5 years. This supposition was found to be incorrect in relation to the pupils studied for these standards. In one community the median 11 year old was only 11.33, and there were many smaller variations.
cells.note: The text reports that the customary half-year age assumption was incorrect, motivating month-level age distributions.

O.outcome_detail: LUS certification after training

cells.quote: The only factor significantly associated with certification was the age of the physician under 40 years (p=0.009). In this group, the certification rate was 85% (95% CI 0.73% to 0.93%), compared with 57% (95% CI 0.41% to 0.72%) among ED physicians aged 40 years or older.
cells.note: Age was an observed learner characteristic, not an instructional treatment; certification required passing both the online quiz and supervised practical assessment.

O.outcome_detail: LUS certification after quiz and supervised practical assessment

cells.quote: As shown in figure 4, the only factor significantly associated with certification was the age of the physician under 40 years (p=0.009). In this group, the certification rate was 85% (95% CI 0.73% to 0.93%), compared with 57% (95% CI 0.41% to 0.72%) among ED physicians aged 40 years or older.
cells.note: Observational subgroup comparison; certification required at least 80% on both the online quiz and supervised practical assessment.

O.outcome_detail: posttraining thoracic anatomy test

cells.quote: After completing the respective training programs, the lung model group demonstrated significantly greater improvement in anatomical understanding, scoring higher in the posttraining test compared with the FLS group (87.60 ± 4.75 vs. 78.19 ± 5.54; p   <  0.001; Table 2 ), indicating superior spatial and procedural anatomical learning.

O.outcome_detail: OSATS during live animal thoracoscopic wedge resection

cells.quote: During the live animal thoracoscopic wedge resection assessment, residents in the lung model group outperformed the FLS group in overall technical skill. The mean OSATS score for the lung model group was significantly higher than that for the FLS group (19.18 ± 2.43 vs. 15.41 ± 2.41; p   <  0.001; Table 2 ).
cells.note: Assessment occurred one week after training; no effect size is printed.

O.outcome_detail: self-reported confidence in thoracoscopic wedge resection

cells.quote: Consistent with the performance outcomes, residents in the lung model group reported significantly greater confidence in performing thoracoscopic wedge resection compared with those in the FLS group (3.13 ± 0.61 vs. 2.27 ± 0.68; p   =  0.002; Table 2 ).
cells.note: Confidence was measured immediately after the live animal procedure; no effect size is printed.

cells.note: The four listed domains favored the lung model group, while stapling showed no significant difference; the latter is coded ns rather than 0 because no equivalence test or adequate-power claim was reported.
